editions.foundations_topic: Resolution, NA, and the k₁ factor
editions.headline: A 149-test CUDA benchmark finds NVIDIA's Compute Sanitizer memcheck reports 18 of the 144 GPU memory-safety violations that apply to it, because its guard regions catch an overflow that lands in dead space and not one that runs into the next live allocation.

ASML and TSMC opened an industry programme to grow the photomask from six inches to twelve, because high-NA EUV's anamorphic optics cut the printed field from 26 × 33 mm to 26 × 16.5 mm and left the largest dies to be stitched from two exposures.

A University of Chicago-led group reports remote epitaxy on metallic and covalently bonded substrates, which a central belief in the field says should not work: the rule for which crystals can grow a peel-off single-crystal film stops being about ionic bonding.

editions.foundations_topic: ENIAC, EDVAC, and the stored-program idea
editions.headline: A quiet weekend in the stack, with no new preprint announcement since Friday and no standards release: the sharpest result standing is Rice University's Einsummable, which models every tensor operation as a relational join and beats hand-tuned PyTorch on an eight-GPU server.

editions.foundations_topic: OPC, phase-shift masks, and inverse lithography
editions.headline: Four researchers re-read 83 microarchitectural side-channel papers from 2014 to 2024 and found 92.8 percent carry at least one full evaluation flaw and 49.4 percent shipped no code, so a decade of attack numbers cannot be ranked against each other.

An ETH Zürich and Czech Academy of Sciences group shows one misplaced soft phonon is why first-principles electro-optic predictions run low: put the measured frequency back and potassium niobate lands at 374 pm/V against 360 ± 30 measured.

editions.foundations_topic: MEMS fabrication: surface versus bulk micromachining
editions.headline: The Optical Internetworking Forum approved CMIS-LT on 2 September: a switch chip and the optical module plugged into it can now negotiate transmitter equalisation over the management bus, instead of both running a setting fixed on a compliance board.

editions.foundations_topic: DRAM: the one-transistor cell, its capacitor, and refresh
editions.headline: DDR5's standardised RowHammer defence turns out to be an attack surface of its own: a paper for RTSS 2026 shows an attacker task priming per-row activation counters can stretch a victim's runtime to 200 percent of its certified worst case.

ASML put production numbers on high-NA EUV at SEMICON Taiwan: ten 0.55-NA scanners running at four customers, 135 wafers an hour at acceptance on an EXE:5200B, and 1.35 million wafers exposed across the fleet.

editions.foundations_topic: Thermal oxidation and the Deal–Grove model
editions.headline: A quiet two days at the end of August: the most consequential thing published is an EPFL circulator that gets 40 decibels of isolation out of ordinary 65-nanometre CMOS by making two leakage paths cancel.

Hot Chips week turned the memory package into the design problem: Samsung is moving the HBM base die to a 4 nm logic process, SK hynix says a 775-micrometre height limit caps the stack, and Intel dropped HBM for 480 GB of LPDDR5X.

The week's biggest numbers shrank on inspection: Applied Materials says cleanroom floor space, not capital, now gates chip capacity, and Nvidia's $105 billion for Ohio turns out to be a lease guaranty rather than financing.
